text:
maya (support): Client reports intermittent 502/503s from our API and their frontend shows no request id. They said its happening in prod for a subset of users. Need minimal repro to escalate.

jordan (support): Short checklist we can send: 1) one curl (or DevTools 'Copy as cURL') that reproduces the failure; 2) HAR or the full response headers block; 3) local time (TZ) of the failure and the route called (e.g. /v1/chat).

maya (support): Pasting a tiny, copy-ready note for non-eng customers so they can reply quickly.

maya (support): "Please attach the smallest thing that reproduces the issue: 1) Open browser DevTools -> Network -> right-click the failing request -> Copy -> Copy as cURL and paste here. 2) If you can export a HAR (Network -> Export HAR) attach it; if not, a screenshot of the request/response headers is fine. 3) Tell us the exact local time (with timezone) when it happened and the endpoint (e.g. /v1/generate)."

jordan (support): For engineers, recommend this curl that returns headers + body so we can see the x-rd-* headers (replace $TOKEN and payload):

jordan (support): ```
# include response headers in output and show SSL handshake
curl -i -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"debug"}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
```

ryan (eng-oncall): If they cannot share the HAR due to PII, ask for the raw response headers block exactly as returned. We can usually correlate a timestamp + x-rd-request-id or x-rd-session-hash. Also suggest toggling SDK debug: JS: set REDWOOD_DEBUG=1 or client.setLogLevel('debug'); Android: LogLevel.DEBUG + capture logs; iOS: enable os_log for networking.

maya (support): Adding tips for mobile / proxied environments (we see these a lot):
- If app sits behind a corporate proxy/WAF, headers may be stripped. Ask them to try a direct curl from a laptop on the same network.
- Android: ask for an `adb logcat` snippet around the time of the failure, or a packet capture using `adb shell tcpdump -w /sdcard/cap.pcap` then pull and attach.
- iOS: request a sysdiagnose (Settings -> Privacy -> Diagnostics & Usage -> Send to App) or reproduce while connected to macOS and run `tcpdump` on the interface.
- React Native / Flutter: capture the embedded webview network logs or run the app on a device/emulator and proxy with mitmproxy to get the full request/response.

jordan (support): If headers are completely missing in client logs, ask them to append this small header echo snippet to the app (or run curl) so we can see what leaves their network:

jordan (support): ```js
// tiny fetch to surface headers (for devs)
fetch('https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer $TOKEN', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ input: 'ping' })
})
  .then(r => r.text().then(body => console.log('STATUS', r.status, 'HEADERS', JSON.stringify(Object.fromEntries(r.headers))), console.log(body)))
```

maya (support): Offer the customer an alternative to pasting artifacts: creating a short-lived debug bundle we can pull. Our preferred CLI for this customer org is `rwdctl` (they may not have it):

maya (support): ```bash
# create a 30m debug bundle from a session hash
rwdctl debug create --session <sessionHash> --ttl 30m
# returns a token string you can paste here for us to fetch internal traces
```

jordan (support): Note: other customers use `rwd support create-debug` in case they only have the support UI. Either way, the token + approximate timestamp lets us pull internal traces inside the SLO window.

ryan (eng-oncall): If they refuse or cannot share anything, propose a quick screenshare so we can watch DevTools + reproduce. Otherwise, ask them to run the curl above from the same network and paste the full stdout (headers + body).

support-bot: Linked incident: https://internal.incidents/INC-2026-189 - attaching this thread for triage :link:

maya (support): Sending this to the customer now and will add any artifacts they send. Tagging @ryan for follow-up if we get a debug token. :white_check_mark:
